summary: The image loader-diag-xnu-ckpt4-usb: NAT-052's loader-diag-xnu-ckpt3-usb with five more kernel stops, C checkpoints 17..21 (after arm_vm_init), built by build.py + patch_ckpt59.py (exact-anchor hunks over the derived ckpt3.c/ckpt3.h; the stub assembly is unchanged and pinned to NAT-052's hash). After arm_vm_init the kernel's TTBR0 becomes *_invalid_ttep; stops 17..21 resume with that table (read by physical address after dc civac), and a C resume with an implausible table holds with mask bit 12 instead of resuming. Plus a session driver (session_nat059.py), a verdict analyser (analyze_nat059.py: 27 note positions ending at checkpoint 21) and decision-draft.md for decision 0025. 20 + 21 tests pass; the mutation check kills 27 of 27 mutants. Nothing ran on the phone and nothing was flashed.
evidence_category: host-test (derivation and static reads of the real payload, a host build of the derived C, driver flow against a fake adb, analyser on model-written archives); not a measurement of the S24

acceptance.2_tests: test_nat059.py (Derivation, Words, Host, Build): the TTBR0 given back is the checkpoint-5 value for every stop up to 16 and the masked *_invalid_ttep for 17..21; implausible or unreadable _invalid_ttep holds with bit 12; the list rule accepts 17..21 and refuses others; the arm_vm_init words and the _set_mmu_ttb routine are decoded from the real payload independently of the patch. The host layer found a product bug (ids 30..44 treated as post-arm_vm_init by 'id >= 17'), fixed with a range rule and a regression test.
acceptance.3_driver_analyser: session_nat059.py is NAT-057's driver with the pins, package path, decision glob, one-shot marker and registry preconditions changed (diff pinned); analyze_nat059.py judges 27 notes n=1..27 incl. the kttbr0 rule; test_nat059_run.py runs both against fake adb and collector-written archives.
acceptance.4_decision_draft: docs/procedures/nat-059/decision-draft.md names both image hashes and decision 0019; no owner confirmation is recorded in it and no native step took place.

established: Host-test: the patch applies to NAT-052's tree, only ckpt3.c/ckpt3.h differ, and the stub assembles to NAT-052's hash.
Static: the end of arm_vm_init in the real payload is set_mmu_ttb(*_invalid_ttep & 0xffffffffffff) and checkpoints 17..21 follow it in arm_init.
Host-test: the derived ckpt3.c resumes stops 17..21 with the masked _invalid_ttep and every earlier stop with the checkpoint-5 value, and refuses to resume when that value is implausible.
Host-test: the analyser separates PASS, PARTIAL, EXCEPTION, BAD_TTBR0/BAD_STATE and undetermined on collector-written archives; the mutation check kills every one of the 27 mutants.
not_established: Anything about the real phone: what the kernel does between checkpoints 16 and 21 is not modelled (arm_vm_init, serial_init, PE_init_platform with vm_initialized, ml_map_cpu_pio, PE_init_cpu, early_random...); static reach is unbounded (3000-5900 functions, indirect calls not followed).
That nothing else changes the kernel's TTBR0 between checkpoints 17 and 21.
That the kernel does not map and access the GIC (GICD 0x10200000, GICR 0x10240000 by the ADT) or other MMIO after vm_initialized; that is disclosed in the decision draft, not excluded.
findings: Checkpoint ids in arm_init are not numerically ordered (10,11,30-35,12,40-44,13-16,[arm_vm_init],17..21): a test 'id >= 17' for 'after arm_vm_init' is wrong for 30..44. The patch uses NAT059_POST_VM(id) = 17 <= id <= 21.
